name: Proxim8 — queue-stress early
description:
Proxim8 is an illustrative 24-hour distributed-inference site in an existing Campbell, California office building sharing a PG&E service with t=0 at local midnight on a business weekday, capped at 5.0 MW. It has 10 Slurm training jobs, 1,000 Kubernetes inference sessions serving Mistral and Cohere LLMs, and 10,000 short Ray agentic API calls; all use hopper_8gpu_air. The seeded workload generator uses seed 20261102. DR-2026-11-02-PROXIM8-MIDNIGHT (PROPOSED_HERE): 5 overnight Kubernetes sessions start at midnight as 24/7 inference carry-over from the previous day. Physical sizing, workload timing, BESS sizing, office PUE, building curve and diesel placeholder are PROPOSED_HERE, illustrative assumptions rather than measured Proxim8 data. DR-2026-11-02-PROXIM8-COOLING (PROPOSED_HERE): non_gpu_load_profile_mw is building non-HVAC electricity (lighting, elevators and tenant plug loads); the existing engine cooling envelope adds modelled HVAC on top without changing alpha_max or other cooling parameters. The curve is scaled using the actual steady-state relation input + alpha_max × lagged input, so at alpha_max=0.2 its input is target/(1+alpha_max): about 0.7 MW total overnight, ramping 6:00–9:00, about 1.6 MW 13:00–17:00, and 0.8 MW by 21:00. A 1.0 MW / 2.0 MWh grid-forming BESS starts at 95% SoC and can recharge from grid headroom; no SoC-floor workaround is needed. No turbines, solar or fuel cells are configured; the diesel block is disabled. The built-in PG&E Schedule B-20 TOU rates are selected with the July calendar month; 114.82 USD/MWh is the flat operating-cost fallback.

Queue-stress early variant (DR-2026-11-03-PROXIM8-QUEUE; DR-2026-11-05-PROXIM8-EARLY-0900, PROPOSED_HERE): the session starts at local 09:00 and the original 24-hour workload and building timelines are rotated by nine hours. Ten hourly inference surges arrive at local 09:15 through 18:15; seeded existing K8S sessions moved to those windows by wave: [150, 120, 100, 100, 160, 100, 80, 70, 60, 55] (995 total). Each retains its original job ID, duration, node count, model identity and hardware profile. The five midnight carry-over sessions rotate to the session's 15:00 mark. The 2,800 original day Ray calls retain their rotated arrival times. A seeded slice of the 7,200 former 16:35 burst calls, [240, 700, 500, 700, 750, 650, 700, 600, 750, 750], is routed through the same cap-admission queue at the ten wave times; the remaining burst calls use seeded weighted random 5-second slots (attempt 1). Slurm jobs retain their rotated starts and ends; a job extending past the 24-hour session boundary is split at t=86,400 s, with the post-boundary remainder outside this run recorded in provenance (PROPOSED_HERE). PG&E B-20 periods still use simulated hours from midnight because the engine has no session-start-hour field, so tariff periods are offset from local clock time by nine hours (PROPOSED_HERE). Seeded target episode durations in seconds are [255, 270, 95, 345, 380, 240, 330, 245, 365, 100]. Six full-day trials calibrated wave 1 and, because wave 1 is shorter than 300 seconds, exactly one other seed-selected long-target wave (wave 5, target 380 seconds). The accepted iteration 6 preserves the committed K8S job membership in all other waves, measures episodes of [60, 130, 85, 115, 300, 115, 100, 85, 95, 85] seconds and stays at or below the 5.0 MW cap.

operating_cost_inputs.diesel_price_usd_per_gal_provenance: Not configured because the diesel block is disabled.
operating_cost_inputs.currency_year_provenance: PROPOSED_HERE: PG&E B-20 rates are in USD; the flat grid price is the operating-cost fallback.

grid_tariff_reference.source: core/economic_dispatch_loop.py pge_price_for_period; Cal. P.U.C. Sheet 61081-E, effective 2026-03-01.

provenance_proxim8.cooling_decision: DR-2026-11-02-PROXIM8-COOLING (PROPOSED_HERE): building HVAC uses the existing engine cooling envelope on top of non-HVAC load.
provenance_proxim8.generation_note: Scripted start/end events only; no kube_config, kube_clusters, or slurm_config.

clock_rotation.edl_time_basis: EDL hour is sim_time_seconds // 3600 % 24; no scenario session-start-hour override exists, so B-20 is 9 hours behind site local time.

ray_background.arrival_shape: weighted independent random arrivals in aligned 5-second slots
ray_background.wave_arrival_shape: seeded former-burst slice; paired arrivals every two seconds

provenance_proxim8_queue_early.slurm_boundary_policy: A rotated job ending after t=86400 has a matching job_end at t=86400; the remaining segment is outside this 24-hour run.

calibration_iteration_log.adjustment: Reduced only wave 1 from 210 to 170 moved K8S sessions.
Raised seeded long-target wave 5 from 100 to 140.
Moved K8S allocation from wave 1 to wave 5; both missed limits.
Moved K8S allocation back toward wave 1; wave 5 remained too long.
Exploratory count candidate; subsequent check found that the sequential allocator changed K8S identities in other waves.
Accepted: preserve all other committed wave identities; transfer 60 sessions from wave 1 to seeded long-target wave 5.

proposed_here: Six logged full-day trials adjusted wave 1 and the seeded long-target fifth wave only.
The seeded duration target of 380 seconds selected wave 5 (13:15 local) as the one additional wave to lengthen after wave 1 became shorter than 300 seconds.
Each moved K8S session keeps its source model, duration, node count and profile.

A seeded slice of the former 7,200-call Ray burst joins the ten cap-gated inference waves; the remainder stays in seeded weighted random 5-second slots, while all 2,800 day calls retain their rotated source arrivals.
A Slurm job crossing the 24-hour boundary ends at the horizon; the remainder is not simulated.
PG&E B-20 clock periods remain offset by nine hours from the site's local clock.
